# Flutter Supabase Doctor — supabase_flutter deep links

> Free, client-side checker that finds why a Supabase Auth OAuth or magic-link deep link never returns to a Flutter app built with supabase_flutter, and gives the exact fix for Info.plist, AndroidManifest.xml, the Supabase dashboard, or your Dart code.

Fill in your app's URL scheme/host, launch mode, flow type, Supabase project URL / Site URL / Redirect URLs allow-list, the OAuth provider, and a few flags about your code, and it works out the exact `scheme://host` your app should register, then cross-checks every layer against it and reports concrete mismatches — no generic advice, no account, no backend.

## What it checks

- **Scheme validity** — empty, reserved (`http`/`https`, which only works via Universal Links / App Links, a separate https-based setup), uppercase letters or whitespace, invalid characters, or an **underscore** in the scheme or host. Google's OAuth redirect handling mangles underscores in redirect URLs, so a scheme or host like `my_app` *always* fails Supabase's redirect-URL check and silently falls back to Site URL — tracked upstream at [supabase/auth#2447](https://github.com/supabase/auth/issues/2447). A hyphen works fine.
- **`redirectTo` vs. `scheme://host`** — whether the value your Dart code passes to `signInWithOAuth()` / `resetPasswordForEmail()` matches the scheme + host you configured, byte-for-byte (a trailing slash alone is enough to break the match).
- **Supabase Redirect URLs allow-list coverage** — matched with the same glob syntax Supabase itself uses (`*`, `**`, `?`, character classes, `\` escapes).
- **Supabase Site URL** — flags `localhost` still set, which is what a rejected redirect silently falls back to, including from production installs.
- **iOS `Info.plist`** — whether `CFBundleURLSchemes` actually lists your scheme; without it iOS never hands the redirect back to your app.
- **Android `AndroidManifest.xml`** — whether an intent-filter exists at all, and whether its `android:scheme` / `android:host` match; also flags `android:autoVerify="true"` left on a custom-scheme filter, which has no effect there (autoVerify only matters for https Android App Links).
- **`authScreenLaunchMode`** — flags `LaunchMode.inAppWebView`, because several providers (Kakao, Discord, Facebook) detect an embedded WebView and either refuse to complete sign-in or never hand control back to the OS to fire the custom-scheme redirect, so the flow just hangs on the provider's page.
- **`authFlowType`** — recommends PKCE over implicit for native apps, since implicit returns the session in a URL fragment that in-app browsers and deep links don't always preserve intact.
- **OAuth provider console** (Google Cloud Console, Apple Services ID, GitHub OAuth App, Discord Developer Portal, Kakao Developers) — whether it has the exact `https://<ref>.supabase.co/auth/v1/callback`, and specifically flags the common mistake of pasting your app's own scheme there instead (the provider redirects to Supabase first; only Supabase then redirects on to your app).
- **`onAuthStateChange` listener** — without one, sign-in can complete while the UI still shows a logged-out screen.

## Who it's for

Flutter developers using `supabase_flutter` for OAuth or magic-link sign-in whose redirect hangs on the provider's page, opens Safari or a Chrome Custom Tab and stops there, or brings the app back to the foreground still signed out — on Android, iOS, or both.

## How it works

Static HTML plus one dependency-free JavaScript file, `doctor-flutter.js`. The page calls a single pure function, `diagnose(config)`, entirely in your browser:

```js
import { diagnose } from './doctor-flutter.js';

const result = diagnose({
  app: {
    scheme, host, androidPackage, iosBundleId,
    launchMode,        // 'externalApplication' | 'inAppWebView' | 'platformDefault' | 'inAppBrowserView' | ''
    authFlowType,       // 'pkce' | 'implicit' | ''
    iosSchemesInPlist,  // string[] — CFBundleURLSchemes as configured
    androidIntentFilter, // { scheme, host, autoVerify }
  },
  supabase: { projectUrl, siteUrl, allowedRedirectUrls },
  provider: { name, authorizedRedirectUris }, // name: 'google'|'apple'|'github'|'discord'|'kakao'|'other'
  code: { redirectTo, usesSkipBrowserRedirect, listensToAuthStateChange },
});
```

There is no backend, no SDK key, and no request that carries your configuration anywhere — read `index.html` and `doctor-flutter.js` directly to verify. It shares its glob-matching logic verbatim with the sibling web and Expo tools, since the allow-list syntax is a Supabase Auth feature identical for every client.

## Worked example

Input — a Flutter app whose Android package and derived URL scheme use an underscore (a very common pattern, since Java/Kotlin package names allow them but URL schemes don't), everything else wired up correctly:

```json
{
  "app": {
    "scheme": "my_app",
    "host": "login-callback",
    "launchMode": "externalApplication",
    "authFlowType": "pkce",
    "iosSchemesInPlist": ["my_app"],
    "androidIntentFilter": { "scheme": "my_app", "host": "login-callback", "autoVerify": false }
  },
  "supabase": {
    "projectUrl": "https://abcd1234.supabase.co",
    "siteUrl": "https://myapp.com",
    "allowedRedirectUrls": ["my_app://**"]
  },
  "provider": {
    "name": "google",
    "authorizedRedirectUris": ["https://abcd1234.supabase.co/auth/v1/callback"]
  },
  "code": {
    "redirectTo": "my_app://login-callback",
    "usesSkipBrowserRedirect": false,
    "listensToAuthStateChange": true
  }
}
```

Output:

```json
{
  "status": "fail",
  "summary": "1 blocking mismatch found. Most urgent: \"my_app\" contains an underscore. Google's OAuth redirect handling mangles underscores in redirect URLs — a scheme or host like \"my_app\" *always* fails Supabase's redirect-URL check and silently falls back to Site URL (tracked in supabase/auth#2447). Use a hyphen instead.",
  "problems": [
    {
      "severity": "high",
      "code": "scheme_underscore",
      "message": "\"my_app\" contains an underscore. Google's OAuth redirect handling mangles underscores in redirect URLs — a scheme or host like \"my_app\" *always* fails Supabase's redirect-URL check and silently falls back to Site URL (tracked in supabase/auth#2447). Use a hyphen instead.",
      "where": "app.scheme"
    }
  ],
  "fixes": [
    { "title": "Replace underscores with hyphens", "value": "my-app", "where": "app.scheme" }
  ],
  "checklist": [
    "Add \"my_app://**\" (covers every path under your scheme) to the Supabase redirect allow-list.",
    "Add \"https://abcd1234.supabase.co/auth/v1/callback\" to \"Authorized redirect URIs\" in Google Cloud Console → APIs & Services → Credentials — exact match, no wildcards.",
    "Use authFlowType: AuthFlowType.pkce and authScreenLaunchMode: LaunchMode.externalApplication together.",
    "Re-run this check after every change — Info.plist, AndroidManifest.xml, and the Supabase/provider consoles drift independently from your Dart code."
  ]
}
```

Every other layer here is wired up consistently — `Info.plist`, the Android intent-filter, the allow-list entry, and the Google Cloud Console callback all agree with each other — so this is a case a manual review would likely wave through. The scheme itself is still silently broken end to end, which is why the tool checks character validity as a standalone, high-severity issue rather than only comparing layers against each other.

## FAQ

**Why does my Supabase OAuth login work in the dashboard but never return to my Flutter app?**
The most common causes, in order: the custom URL scheme has an invalid character (especially an underscore, which Google's OAuth redirect handling silently mangles); `Info.plist` or the `AndroidManifest.xml` intent-filter don't actually register the scheme your code uses; the value isn't covered by the Supabase Redirect URLs allow-list; or `authScreenLaunchMode` is `LaunchMode.inAppWebView`, which several providers refuse to complete inside.

**Why does an underscore in my app's URL scheme break Google sign-in with Supabase?**
Google's OAuth redirect handling strips or otherwise mangles underscores in the redirect URL it sends back, so a scheme like `my_app://callback` never matches what's on Supabase's Redirect URLs allow-list — Supabase then falls back to Site URL instead, which is often still `localhost` or the wrong domain. This is documented in [supabase/auth#2447](https://github.com/supabase/auth/issues/2447); the fix is to use a hyphen (`my-app://callback`) instead.

**What redirect URI do I put in Google Cloud Console for a Supabase + Flutter app?**
Supabase's own callback, `https://<your-project-ref>.supabase.co/auth/v1/callback` — not your app's custom scheme. In the OAuth handshake, Google redirects to Supabase first; only after Supabase processes that does it redirect on to your app's `scheme://host`. Pasting your app's scheme into the provider console instead of Supabase's callback is one of the most common configuration mistakes.

**Why does Kakao (or Discord, or Facebook) login hang on the provider's page in a Flutter app?**
These providers detect when they're running inside an embedded WebView and either refuse to complete sign-in or never hand control back to the OS to fire your app's custom-scheme redirect — so with `authScreenLaunchMode: LaunchMode.inAppWebView` the flow just stalls. Switch to `LaunchMode.externalApplication` so the OS opens a real browser (or Custom Tab / SFSafariViewController), which can actually trigger the redirect back to your app.

**Does `android:autoVerify="true"` do anything for a custom URL scheme intent-filter?**
No. `autoVerify` only triggers Digital Asset Links verification for Android App Links, which use `https` and require a hosted `assetlinks.json`. On a custom-scheme intent-filter (e.g. `myapp://`) it is silently ignored — leaving it there just invites confusion later when someone assumes it's doing something.

**Should I use PKCE or implicit flow with supabase_flutter?**
PKCE, which is the `supabase_flutter` default. Implicit flow returns the session in a URL fragment (`#access_token=...`), and in-app browsers, Custom Tabs, and some deep-link paths don't always preserve a URL fragment intact end to end. PKCE instead returns a short-lived `?code=` that's exchanged for a session, which is more robust across the exact hop your OAuth redirect takes.

**Why does my UI still show a logged-out screen even though the deep link reached my app?**
`supabase_flutter` parses the session from the incoming deep link automatically, but nothing updates your UI without your own listener. Add `supabase.auth.onAuthStateChange.listen((data) { ... })` (typically near app startup) and update navigation/state from there — otherwise sign-in can complete internally while the screen never reflects it.

## Privacy

No account, no login, no cookies for the tool itself, no server-side processing of your config. The only analytics are anonymous usage counts (event name + count, never the content of what you entered) sent to a self-hosted Umami instance.
